question: Which of these is a coordinating conjunction commonly used to connect two similar or equal ideas together? 🔗
explanation: Excellent! 'And' is a coordinating conjunction that joins words, phrases, or sentences that have equal importance, like 'apples AND oranges'! ➕
hint: It is the 'A' in the FANBOYS acronym.

question: Which conjunction is best used to show a contrast or difference between two ideas? ⚖️
explanation: Awesome! 'But' is the perfect word to show contrast, like in the sentence 'I like cake, BUT I don't like pie.' 🛑
hint: It is the 'B' in FANBOYS.

question: If you are giving someone a choice between two things, which conjunction should you use? 🤔
explanation: Fantastic! 'Or' gives a choice or option, like asking 'Do you want tea OR juice?' 🔀
hint: It is the 'O' in FANBOYS.

question: Which conjunction shows the result or consequence of an action? 🏁
explanation: Brilliant! 'So' shows a result. For example, 'It was raining, SO I took my umbrella.' ➡️
hint: It is the 'S' in FANBOYS.

question: What does the famous acronym 'FANBOYS' help us remember? 🧠
explanation: Super! FANBOYS stands for For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So—the seven coordinating conjunctions! 🤝
hint: These words join equal parts of a sentence together.

question: Which conjunction works just like 'because' to show a reason in the FANBOYS family? 🕵️‍♂️
explanation: Great job! 'For' can mean 'because'. For example: 'I drank water, FOR I was very thirsty.' 🎁
hint: It is the 'F' in FANBOYS.

question: Which conjunction is used to connect two negative ideas together? 🙅‍♂️
explanation: Perfect! 'Nor' joins two negative choices. Example: 'He doesn't like spinach, NOR does he like broccoli.' 🚫
hint: It starts with an 'N' and pairs well with 'neither'.

question: Which word is a subordinating conjunction that shows the 'reason' why something happened? 💡
explanation: Wonderful! 'Because' introduces a dependent clause that explains the reason, like 'I smiled BECAUSE I was happy.' 🧠
hint: It answers the question 'Why?'

question: Conjunctions that work together in pairs, like 'either/or', are called what? 👯
explanation: Spot on! Correlative conjunctions are 'relatives' that always travel in pairs to connect parts of a sentence! 💞
hint: The word starts with 'Corre...'.

question: What is the missing word in this correlative pair: 'Either... ____'? 🤷‍♀️
explanation: Excellent! 'Either' always partners with 'Or'. For example: 'You can have EITHER chocolate OR vanilla.' 🔀
hint: It gives you a choice.

question: What is the missing word in this correlative pair: 'Neither... ____'? 🙅‍♀️
explanation: Awesome! 'Neither' always partners with 'Nor' to show two negative options. 🚫
hint: It rhymes with 'or' but starts with an 'N'.

question: What is the missing word in this correlative pair: 'Both... ____'? 🤝
explanation: Fantastic! 'Both' and 'And' team up to include two things, like 'BOTH dogs AND cats make great pets.' ➕
hint: It is the 'A' in FANBOYS.

question: What is the missing phrase in this correlative pair: 'Not only... ____'? ✨
explanation: Brilliant! 'Not only' goes with 'but also'. Example: 'She is NOT ONLY smart BUT ALSO very kind.' 🌟
hint: It starts with 'but'.

question: What is the missing word in this correlative pair: 'Whether... ____'? ⚖️
explanation: Great job! 'Whether' always pairs with 'or', like 'I don't know WHETHER to laugh OR cry.' 🔀
hint: It is the same word that pairs with 'either'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I wanted to play outside, ____ it started to rain.' 🌧️
explanation: Super! 'But' is the perfect fit here because it shows the contrast between wanting to play and the rain stopping you. 🛑
hint: You need a word that shows opposite or unexpected ideas.

question: Fill in the blank: 'We can go to the movies, ____ we can stay home and play games.' 🎲
explanation: Perfect! 'Or' gives us two fun choices to pick from. 🔀
hint: Which word shows a choice between two options?

question: Fill in the blank: 'I was very tired, ____ I went to bed early.' 🛏️
explanation: Wonderful! 'So' tells us the result of being tired—going to bed early! ➡️
hint: Which word shows a result?

question: Fill in the blank: 'He studied hard, ____ he still failed the test.' 📝
explanation: Spot on! 'Yet' shows a surprise or contrast, similar to 'but'. He studied, YET he failed. 😲
hint: It is the 'Y' in FANBOYS.

question: Fill in the blank: 'She loves to paint, ____ she also loves to draw.' 🎨
explanation: Awesome! 'And' simply adds more information. She loves to paint AND draw. ➕
hint: It connects two similar, positive ideas.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I will not eat broccoli, ____ will I eat spinach.' 🥦
explanation: Excellent! 'Nor' is used to connect two things you will NOT do. 🚫
hint: It is the negative cousin of 'or'.

question: Which of these is a Subordinating conjunction? 📉
explanation: Fantastic! 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction because it introduces a dependent clause. 🤷‍♂️
hint: It is the only word here that isn't in FANBOYS.

question: Fill in the blank with a subordinating conjunction: '____ it was raining, we still went for a walk.' 🚶‍♂️
explanation: Brilliant! 'Although' introduces the surprising fact that you went for a walk despite the rain! ☔
hint: It means 'Even though'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'You cannot watch television ____ you finish your homework.' 📺
explanation: Great job! 'Unless' sets a condition. You have to finish homework first! 🚫
hint: It means 'except if'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'We will go to the park ____ the sun comes out.' ☀️
explanation: Super! 'If' creates a condition. The sun has to come out for the park trip to happen. 🤔
hint: It is a tiny two-letter word.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Please wash your hands ____ you eat dinner.' 🧼
explanation: Perfect! 'Before' tells us the time order. Hand washing comes first! ⏪
hint: It means earlier in time.

question: Fill in the blank: 'You can have dessert ____ you finish your vegetables.' 🥦
explanation: Wonderful! 'After' shows that the veggies must be eaten first, then comes dessert! ⏩
hint: It means later in time.

question: Fill in the blank: '____ I was walking to school, I saw a beautiful bird.' 🐦
explanation: Spot on! 'While' tells us two things were happening at the exact same time. ⏳
hint: It relates to time passing during an event.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I have been playing the piano ____ I was five years old.' 🎹
explanation: Awesome! 'Since' points back to a specific starting time in the past. 📅
hint: It shows when something started.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Keep running ____ you reach the finish line!' 🏁
explanation: Excellent! 'Until' tells you to keep doing an action up to a certain point in time. 🛑
hint: It means 'up to the time that'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I will call you ____ I arrive at the station.' 🚉
explanation: Fantastic! 'When' connects the action of calling to the specific time of arriving. ⏰
hint: It relates to time.

question: What type of conjunction connects an independent clause with a dependent clause? 🚂
explanation: Brilliant! Subordinating conjunctions (like because, if, when) attach a weaker dependent clause to a strong independent clause! 📉
hint: Think of the word 'subordinate' meaning 'lower in rank'.

question: Which sentence uses a Correlative conjunction correctly? 💞
options: Either clean your room or do the dishes. 🧹
Because you cleaned, you can play. 🎮
I cleaned, so I can play. ⚽
answer: Either clean your room or do the dishes. 🧹
explanation: Great job! 'Either... or' is a correlative pair that works together beautifully! 🧹
hint: Look for the sentence with a matching pair of conjunctions.

question: Which of these words is NOT a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS)? 🕵️‍♀️
explanation: Super! 'Because' is a subordinating conjunction, not a coordinating one! 🧠
hint: Think of the acronym FANBOYS.

question: Fill in the blank with a correlative conjunction: 'The movie was ____ long, but also very boring.' 🥱
explanation: Perfect! 'Not only' goes hand-in-hand with 'but also'. 🌟
hint: Look at the second part of the sentence: 'but also'.

question: Fill in the blank: '____ my brother and my sister are older than me.' 👨‍👩‍👧
explanation: Wonderful! 'Both' pairs with 'and' to include two people! 🤝
hint: Look at the word 'and' later in the sentence.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I don't know ____ we are having pizza or pasta for dinner.' 🍕
explanation: Spot on! 'Whether' pairs with 'or' when you are thinking about two possibilities. ⚖️
hint: It sounds like the word for sunny/rainy, but spelled differently.

question: Fill in the blank: '____ Mark nor Jake knew the answer.' 🤷‍♂️
explanation: Awesome! 'Neither' always partners with 'nor' for negative choices. 🙅‍♂️
hint: Look at the word 'nor' later in the sentence.

question: What kind of conjunction is the word 'since'? 📅
explanation: Excellent! 'Since' is a subordinating conjunction that can show time or reason. 📉
hint: It makes a clause dependent.

question: Identify the conjunction in this sentence: 'I wore a jacket because it was snowing.' ❄️
explanation: Fantastic! 'Because' is the conjunction that joins the two ideas together. 🧠
hint: It is the word that explains 'why'.

question: Identify the conjunction in this sentence: 'Would you like to play soccer or basketball?' 🏀
explanation: Brilliant! 'Or' is the conjunction connecting the two sport choices. 🔀
hint: It is the word that gives a choice.

question: What is the job of a conjunction in a sentence? 👷‍♂️
options: To join words, phrases, or clauses 🔗
answer: To join words, phrases, or clauses 🔗
explanation: Great job! Conjunctions are like glue; their main job is to connect different parts of a sentence together! 🔗
hint: Think of a conjunction as a bridge.

question: Which conjunction best completes this sentence: 'I like cats, ____ I am allergic to them.' 🐈
explanation: Super! 'But' is perfect here because it shows the sad contrast between liking cats and being allergic. 🛑
hint: You need a word that shows a problem or contrast.

question: Which conjunction best completes this sentence: 'It is very cold outside, ____ wear a warm coat.' 🧥
explanation: Perfect! 'So' shows that wearing a coat is the result of it being cold outside! ➡️
hint: You need a word that shows a result.

question: Which pair of correlative conjunctions fits best: 'You can have ____ a cookie ____ a brownie, but not both.' 🍪
explanation: Wonderful! 'Either / or' is used because you are allowed to choose only one of the sweet treats! 🔀
hint: You have a choice between two positive things.

question: Which pair fits best: '____ the coach ____ the players were happy with the referee’s decision.' 😠
explanation: Spot on! 'Neither / nor' works perfectly to show that zero people were happy. 🙅‍♂️
hint: It means 'not this one, and not that one'.

question: Fill in the blank with a subordinating conjunction: 'I will help you with your homework ____ you help me clean my room.' 🧹
explanation: Awesome! 'If' creates a fair deal or condition between two people! 🤔
hint: It sets a condition.

question: Fill in the blank: '____ I love ice cream, I can't eat it every single day.' 🍦
explanation: Excellent! 'Even though' introduces a contrasting dependent clause, similar to 'although'. 🤷‍♀️
hint: It means 'despite the fact that'.

question: What punctuation mark is usually placed right before a coordinating conjunction that joins two complete sentences? 📝
explanation: Fantastic! When joining two independent clauses with a FANBOYS conjunction, you should always use a comma right before it! ✍️
hint: It represents a short pause.

question: Identify the type of conjunction used here: 'She went to the library SO she could study in peace.' 📚
explanation: Brilliant! 'So' is one of the seven coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS)! 🤝
hint: Think of the famous acronym!

question: Identify the type of conjunctions used here: 'He is NOT ONLY a great singer BUT ALSO a fantastic dancer.' 🕺
explanation: Great job! 'Not only... but also' is a pair of correlative conjunctions working together as a team! 💞
hint: They come in a pair!
